Building smarter, faster in Hong Kong
body:
Facing a chronic labour shortage and soaring construction costs, Hong Kong’s infrastructure sector is turning to advanced materials, technical innovation and standardised quality assurance to speed up constructions works.

 

Leading this effort is the Building Technology Research Institute (BTRi), established in August 2024 and wholly owned by the Financial Secretary Incorporated. Since its inception, the BTRi has advanced more than 45 innovative initiatives to modernise local practices towards high-efficiency development.

 

Pioneering concrete

An embankment at Yuen Long’s Shap Pat Heung Interchange has become Hong Kong’s first roadwork project to deploy Low Density Engineered Cementitious Composites (LD-ECC).

 

Despite its appearance as ordinary concrete, the locally developed material boasts higher compressive strength at roughly a quarter of traditional concrete’s weight and density, alongside self-healing micro-cracks properties and enhanced fatigue resistance.

 

Civil Engineering & Development Department (CEDD) Engineer Derrick Kwok explained that the team used 400mm x 400mm LD-ECC precast panels to build the permanent formwork before filling the interior with the material.

 

“It has completely transformed Hong Kong’s traditional retaining wall design, which relies on reinforced concrete. LD-ECC precast panels are relatively light,” Mr Kwok said.

 

“Workers do not need to lift heavy loads during assembly, which reduces the risk of injury.”

 

Slashing costs

He added that the new approach minimises heavy, noisy machinery, making it particularly well-suited for Hong Kong’s dense, space-constrained construction sites.

 

“The LD-ECC lightweight filling method eliminated complex workflows such as scaffolding, formwork and fixing reinforcement. The project construction time was cut by 50% and direct building costs dropped by 20%.”

 

Throughout the project, technical document reviews by the BTRi supported the team in transitioning this innovative material to real-world application.

 

New guidelines

To drive wider adoption, the CEDD has commissioned the BTRi to draft technical guidelines for LD-ECC, slated for release in the second quarter of 2027.

 

According to BTRi's Deputy Section Head (Standards Advancement) Edwin Tang, the forthcoming guidelines will be highly comprehensive.

 

“They will cover the definition of LD-ECC, raw material performance specifications, testing standards, structural design methodologies, construction procedures and quality control requirements,” Mr Tang said.

 

He noted that the guidelines will serve as a key reference standard for future civil engineering projects.

 

“They are particularly applicable to road expansion works in constrained sites, lightweight backfilling and fast-track infrastructure projects with tight commissioning schedules,” Mr Tang said.

 

Driving innovation

The BTRi drives construction innovation through three core missions: leading research and development for innovative materials like LD-ECC, advancing standards, and providing accreditation, certification and testing for construction products and Modular Integrated Construction manufacturers.

 

“To date, the BTRi has undertaken more than 45 innovation initiatives, which are projected to save the construction industry up to $3.1 billion annually,” said BTRi’s Chief Executive Officer Alfred Wong.

 

The 2026-27 Budget earmarked $100 million for the BTRi to conduct various studies, with a focus on updating construction standards and integrating artificial intelligence applications into construction projects.

 

“As new technologies, materials and construction machinery emerge, existing standards may not adequately address them,” said Mr Wong.

 

“To bridge this gap, we are developing dedicated technical guidelines, while harmonising regional standards with the Greater Bay Area. These efforts will provide the construction industry with a clear and reliable framework for the wider adoption of innovation.”

 

Mr Wong added that the institute plans to establish a benchmark assessment mechanism for artificial intelligence applications to ensure new solutions strictly align with government public works standards.

title: HSK Logistics Cluster interest invited
body:
The Transport & Logistics Bureau, in collaboration with the Civil Engineering & Development Department, today invited market expressions of interest (EOI) to develop selected land parcels for a modern logistics cluster (HSK Logistics Cluster) in the Hung Shui Kiu/Ha Tsuen New Development Area.

 

The five selected sites, ranging from 3.1 to 5 hectares, were identified following a preliminary market sounding exercise. They comprise three parcels in Zone B, which focuses on e-commerce logistics, one in Zone A, focused on high-value goods logistics, and one in Zone C, which focuses on freight forwarding and the low-altitude economy.

 

Development will be implemented in phases with Zone B forming the first batch. The three parcels within Zone B will become available by late 2027 or early 2028 at the earliest. If combined, they can cater to larger-scale development. The single land parcels in Zones A and C will be made available at a later stage.

 

Through this EOI exercise, the Government aims to gauge industry interest in developing the first five available sites within the HSK Logistics Cluster. It is also seeking views on the proposed development terms, infrastructure requirements, development scenarios, land disposal options and financial viability.

 

The feedback collected will help the Government formulate the land lease terms and development mode.

 

The deadline for EOI submissions is noon on November 13. A briefing session will be held on September 11, with details available on the  HSK Logistics Cluster webpage.

title: Autonomous vehicles trial approved
body:
The Transport Department (TD) today announced that it has issued a pilot licence for autonomous vehicles (AVs), approving a trial between the Express Rail Link at Hong Kong West Kowloon Station and the Airport Express at Kowloon Station.

 

Issued in accordance with the Road Traffic (Autonomous Vehicles) Regulation, the pilot licence approves the trial of four private cars operating in autonomous mode. The approved route includes Wui Man Road, Jordan Road, Nga Cheung Road and Station Perimeter Roads South, East and North.

 

A backup operator will remain inside each vehicle to take control if needed. Additionally, all participating AVs must display the TD's designated labels for public awareness.

 

The department noted that the trial will test AV technology safety, stability and operational feasibility in high passenger flows and complex traffic dynamics. Success in this multimodal transport hub will help integrate autonomous fleets into the wider public transport network.

 

Once regular operations begin, the AVs will provide a seamless, automated interchange between the Express Rail Link and the Airport Express. This convenient connection is expected to attract more travellers to use both the Express Rail Link and Hong Kong International Airport.

 

Chaired by the Commissioner for Transport, the Autonomous Vehicle Applications Promotion Working Group will monitor the project. The group will collaborate with relevant departments and the industry to review the progress of each AV project. The group will also guide trial locations, vehicle types and licensing frameworks to support commercial development, while exploring regulatory arrangements for limited commercial services.

title: Opportunities explored in Malaysia
body:
Secretary for Commerce & Economic Development Algernon Yau today led a business delegation to explore new economic opportunities in Malaysia.

 

The group includes representatives from Mainland enterprises, Hong Kong chambers of commerce and other key industry organisations. The visit was organised by the Task Force on Supporting Mainland Enterprises in Going Global, which is jointly led by Mr Yau and Invest Hong Kong.

 

The visit began with a business seminar and networking lunch hosted by Invest Hong Kong. The event provided Mainland delegates with direct networking access to potential Malaysian business partners.

 

Delivering his opening remarks, Mr Yau highlighted Hong Kong’s strategic role as a "super connector" and a "super value-adder" that links capital and opportunities between the East and the West. “With this strategic role, coupled with the many strengths of Hong Kong, Hong Kong is prepared to serve as the ideal springboard linking the Chinese Mainland and Malaysia,” he said.

 

On the sidelines of the seminar, Invest Hong Kong signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with the Malaysian Investment Development Authority to deepen bilateral co-operation. The signing was witnessed by Mr Yau and Malaysia’s Deputy Minister of Investment, Trade & Industry.

  

Director-General of Investment Promotion Alpha Lau described the trip as a major success in helping Mainland enterprises leverage Hong Kong to expand into Malaysia and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) market. She noted that the delegation attended the Hong Kong Trade Development Council’s “Think Business, Think Hong Kong” event to meet local business leaders.

 

“Malaysia being a very key economy within the ASEAN region, we arranged for them to meet not only the government agencies, but also to meet potential key partners.

 

“More ASEAN companies are now also using Hong Kong as a platform to expand further into the Greater Bay Area, or the Chinese Mainland as a whole, and some of them even use Hong Kong to further develop their business in the rest of the world,” she added.

 

Mainland delegates hailed the trip as fruitful.

 

Communications executive Athena Zhao called the task force an accelerator for companies going global, noting its help in connecting businesses with crucial legal and financial services.

 

Mainland technology executive Max Zhao added that official government endorsement provided direct access to senior-level local counterparts.

 

In the afternoon, the delegation visited Ant International to learn about digital solutions empowering small and medium-sized enterprises in Malaysia. They exchanged views on fostering partnerships via Hong Kong with Antom Senior Vice President and Chief Executive Officer Gary Liu.

 

The group also visited Hong Leong Manufacturing Group, one of Malaysia’s largest diversified conglomerates, to discuss market strategies with Group President Kwek Leng San.

 

In the evening, Mr Yau held a dinner meeting with Malaysia’s Deputy Minister of Finance Liew Chin Tong to discuss economic trends and exchange views on strengthening co-operation between Hong Kong, Malaysia and ASEAN.

 

Mr Yau will attend an MOU signing ceremony between the competition commissions of Hong Kong and Malaysia tomorrow before returning to Hong Kong.

title: HK office in Kuala Lumpur opens
body:
Secretary for Commerce & Economic Development Algernon Yau today officiated at the official opening ceremony of the Hong Kong Economic and Trade Office (ETO) in Kuala Lumpur during his visit to Malaysia.

 

The opening marks a significant milestone in deepening partnerships between Hong Kong and Malaysia, and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) as a whole.

 

Addressing the opening ceremony, Mr Yau highlighted the strategic importance of this office, which is the 15th overseas ETO of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government and the fourth in the ASEAN region.

 

Mr Yau noted that ASEAN stands firmly as Hong Kong's second-largest trading partner in goods while Malaysia is the city's eighth largest trading partner. He added that the new ETO shoulders the responsibility of deepening Hong Kong's economic, trade and investment ties with this strategically important region and strengthening the city’s presence in it.

 

The geographical coverage of the Kuala Lumpur ETO includes Malaysia, Brunei Darussalam, Laos and Pakistan.

 

Mr Yau also led a business delegation to attend the "Think Business, Think Hong Kong" symposium and luncheon organised by the Hong Kong Trade Development Council (HKTDC).

 

The business delegates, including representatives from Mainland enterprises looking to go global, Hong Kong chambers of commerce and other organisations, held exchange sessions with the Malaysia Digital Economy Corporation and local chambers to gain a deeper understanding of the situation and needs of the Malaysian market.

 

Speaking at the symposium, Mr Yau said that amid the profound transformation in the global economy characterised by geopolitical tensions, supply chain realignments and technological changes, Hong Kong, with its core strengths, can be Malaysia's partner to navigate the increasingly complex external environment.

 

He noted that Hong Kong's unique strength lies not only in its robust infrastructure or business-friendly policies, but also in its unmatched connectivity with the Mainland and the rest of the world, empowering Hong Kong to serve the Malaysian business community as a “super connector” and “super value-adder”.

 

Mr Yau said that Malaysian businesses can readily gain access to the Mainland market, particularly the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, via Hong Kong. Concurrently, the Hong Kong SAR Government’s Task Force on Supporting Mainland Enterprises in Going Global provides one-stop, customised services to help Mainland firms invest directly in overseas markets like Malaysia, creating a win-win outcome.

 

He identified new opportunities for bilateral collaboration in innovation, technology and green development, noting that Hong Kong and Malaysia are strategic partners in shaping future economies.

 

During the event, Mr Yau witnessed the signing of Memorandums of Understanding between four Hong Kong media organisations and Malaysian media and other organisations to foster new partnerships. The HKTDC also signed agreements with local chambers of commerce and related institutions to strengthen collaboration.
